title: MS Dhoni's winning six — 2011 World Cup Final
original_line: Dhoni finishes off in style! A magnificent strike into the crowd! India lift the World Cup after 28 years! And the celebrations have started in the Indian dressing room — it's an emotional moment.
context: Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai. Chasing Sri Lanka's 274, India's captain MS Dhoni promotes himself up the order and seals the title with a towering six over long-on. India's first World Cup since 1983; Sachin Tendulkar's home crowd erupts.

title: England win the 2019 World Cup on a super over
original_line: England have won the World Cup! By the barest of margins! By the barest of all margins! Absolute ecstasy for England, agony for New Zealand!
context: Lord's, London. The final and the super over both tie; England win on boundary count after a run-out at the non-striker's end. The most dramatic finish in World Cup history.

title: Carlos Brathwaite's four sixes — 2016 World T20 Final
original_line: Carlos Brathwaite! Carlos Brathwaite! Remember the name!
context: Eden Gardens, Kolkata. West Indies need 19 off the final over against England; Brathwaite hits Ben Stokes for four consecutive sixes to win the title.

title: Shane Warne's 'Ball of the Century' to Mike Gatting — 1993 Ashes
original_line: He's done it! Gatting has absolutely no idea what has happened to it. He still doesn't know.
context: Old Trafford, Manchester. Warne's first ball in Ashes cricket drifts well outside leg stump and rips back to clip the top of off — bamboozling Mike Gatting. The delivery that announced Warne to the world.

title: India win the inaugural World T20 — 2007 Final
original_line: Sreesanth takes it! India have won the World Twenty20! Misbah's improvised scoop finds the man at short fine leg, and the young Indian side are champions of the world!
context: Wanderers, Johannesburg. Pakistan need 6 off the last ball; Misbah-ul-Haq attempts a scoop off Joginder Sharma and is caught by Sreesanth. India win MS Dhoni's first global title.

title: Kapil Dev's running catch to dismiss Viv Richards — 1983 World Cup Final
original_line: And Richards has gone! Kapil Dev, running back from midwicket, holds on — and that could be the turning point of this final!
context: Lord's. Defending a modest 183, Kapil Dev sprints back over his shoulder to catch a dangerous Viv Richards. India go on to stun the mighty West Indies for their first World Cup.

title: Allan Donald run out — 1999 World Cup Semi-Final tie
original_line: They've gone for the run — Donald's stranded! The stumps are broken! It's a tie, and Australia go through! Unbelievable scenes at Edgbaston!
context: Edgbaston. With scores level and one needed, a mix-up leaves Allan Donald stranded mid-pitch; Australia run him out to tie the match and advance to the final on net run rate. South African heartbreak.

title: VVS Laxman's 281 — Kolkata Test 2001
original_line: This is batting from another planet — Laxman, so wristy, so serene, has taken the game away from Australia after following on. We are watching one of the great innings of all time.
context: Eden Gardens. Following on against Steve Waugh's all-conquering Australia, Laxman (281) and Dravid bat all day to script one of cricket's greatest comebacks; India win from nowhere.

title: Ben Stokes' miracle at Headingley — 2019 Ashes
original_line: Stokes has done it! He has dragged England to the most improbable victory! One of the greatest innings of all time — Headingley belongs to Ben Stokes!
context: Headingley, Leeds. England, chasing 359 with one wicket left, watch Ben Stokes (135*) farm the strike and blaze the winning runs with Jack Leach for company to keep the Ashes alive.

title: Yuvraj Singh's six sixes in an over — 2007 World T20
original_line: That's six sixes! Yuvraj Singh has taken Stuart Broad apart — every single ball into the stands! Astonishing power and audacity!
context: Kingsmead, Durban. Fired up after words with Andrew Flintoff, Yuvraj Singh smashes Stuart Broad for six sixes in one over and reaches a fifty in 12 balls.

title: AB de Villiers' 31-ball ODI hundred — 2015
original_line: He's done it in 31 balls — the fastest hundred in one-day history! AB de Villiers is rewriting what is possible with a cricket bat!
context: Johannesburg. Against the West Indies, AB de Villiers reaches the fastest ODI century ever off just 31 balls, hitting it to all parts in a breathtaking assault.

title: Javed Miandad's last-ball six — Sharjah 1986
original_line: Miandad swings — and it's gone, all the way! A six off the last ball! Pakistan have won it, and Sharjah has gone wild!
context: Sharjah. Needing four off the final ball of the Austral-Asia Cup final against India, Javed Miandad launches Chetan Sharma for six — an iconic moment in Pakistan cricket folklore.

title: Wasim Akram's two-in-two — 1992 World Cup Final
original_line: What a delivery! And again! Wasim Akram has produced two of the most magical balls you'll ever see — England are reeling!
context: MCG, Melbourne. In the final, Wasim Akram dismisses Allan Lamb and Chris Lewis with consecutive unplayable deliveries to swing the match decisively Pakistan's way.

title: Sachin Tendulkar's 'Desert Storm' — Sharjah 1998
original_line: What a player! Tendulkar, against the wind and the sandstorm and the best attack in the world — this is simply magnificent batting!
context: Sharjah. Amid a literal sandstorm, Sachin Tendulkar produces back-to-back masterclasses against Australia to drag India into the final and then win it on his birthday.

title: Adam Gilchrist's 149 — 2007 World Cup Final
original_line: Gilchrist is taking this final apart — 149 of the most destructive batting you'll ever see in a World Cup final!
context: Kensington Oval, Barbados. Adam Gilchrist blasts 149 off 104 balls (famously with a squash ball in his glove) to power Australia to a third straight World Cup title in a rain-shortened final.
